project.name: Open Data Explorer
project.core_thesis: Public-data access is not the main problem. The harder problem is turning a civic question into a defensible evidence architecture: discovering relevant datasets, understanding their roles, validating whether they can actually work together, and recommending an appropriate representation of the result.
project.positioning_sentence: Open Data Explorer turns civic questions into validated evidence workflows: discover what data fits, test how it can actually work together, execute selected relationships, and recommend the right form for the result.

product_principles: Start with what the user wants to understand or build, not with dataset names.
The official catalogue and source data remain canonical; AI is never the evidence source.
Semantic relevance does not prove analytical compatibility.
Candidate relationships must remain distinguishable from schema-observed, sample-validated and execution-validated relationships.
Missing or external evidence must be represented explicitly.
The graph or visualization is a projection of structured evidence, not the source of truth.
The public prototype should be useful without requiring an LLM, API key, Worker or backend.
Generative compute should preferably remain on the user's side; the platform provides evidence, method and representation intelligence.

showcase_prototype.goal: Create a compelling public prototype suitable for submission to the Basel-Stadt Open Data Showcase portal.
scope: load the complete live Basel-Stadt catalogue in the browser
provide a better searchable and inspectable index than the source portal
offer an Atlas view that makes the catalogue navigable through meaningful projections
accept a natural-language civic use case
build a proposed evidence plan with direct, supporting, contextual and missing evidence
inspect real dataset structure and provenance
validate selected spatial relationships against real data
recommend useful ways to represent the result
render a small set of client-side visualization templates

levels.name: Catalogue
levels.question: What data exists?
capabilities: direct search by id, title, description, publisher, keyword and theme

levels.name: Atlas
levels.question: How can I navigate the public-data landscape?

levels.name: Discover evidence
levels.question: Which evidence fits my use case?
capabilities: direct, supporting, contextual and missing classes

levels.name: Compose and validate
levels.question: Can these datasets actually work together?
capabilities: spatial join, nearest, aggregation and incompatibility proposals
confirmed, rejected, partial and failed outcomes

levels.name: Represent
levels.question: What is the right form for this result?
capabilities: recommend map, chart, table, comparison cards, brief or reusable data output
bind executed result fields to visualization templates
explain why a representation fits the data and user intent

levels.name: Generate
levels.question: How is that representation instantiated?
capabilities: optional LLM-host generation from a structured representation specification
standalone HTML or application output where appropriate

atlas.purpose: Make the complete catalogue feel like navigable terrain rather than an administrative list or an undifferentiated force graph.
atlas.design_reference: GitHub Atlas interaction grammar: maps over lists, curated lenses, drill-down and signal over noise.

primary_taxonomy_strategy.principle: The topical taxonomy should be induced from the actual Basel catalogue rather than imposed as a generic universal category tree.
primary_taxonomy_strategy.method: Use deterministic metadata rules where confidence is high; optionally use an LLM to classify ambiguous records and help induce or refine category boundaries.
primary_taxonomy_strategy.provenance_rule: LLM category assignments are model inference, never source metadata.

output.origin: source, deterministic system inference or model inference

projections.label: Civic theme
projections.question: What is the data about?
projections.note: Example labels are scaffolding only; final categories and counts should be derived from the live corpus.

projections.label: Space
projections.question: What spatial form does this dataset describe?

projections.label: Time
projections.question: How does this dataset relate to time?
projections.rule: Do not label a dataset historical or archived merely because it is old; require supporting metadata or observed temporal structure.

projections.label: Readiness
projections.question: How usable is this dataset for analysis?

projections.label: Analytical use
projections.question: What kinds of analytical roles can this dataset play?

projections.label: This question
projections.question: How does the catalogue reorganize around the active use case?

interaction.default: hierarchical atlas categories, not all datasets in one live force simulation
interaction.d3_role: render deliberate projections of the same canonical catalogue, with stable layouts rather than continuously drifting nodes

available_now: record count and temporal coverage where available

landing_panel.title: Recently updated
landing_panel.source: sort live catalogue by modified timestamp
landing_panel.rule: Do not call modified datasets new unless a reliable creation timestamp is available.

future_optional_worker.not_needed_for: showing current live catalogue or current recently modified datasets

intelligence_boundary.hybrid_indexing_rule: Algorithmic by default, semantic escalation when uncertain.

representation_layer.principle: The orchestrator should recommend and describe representations, while rendering/generative compute can happen in the client or user's LLM host.

mcp_end_state.role: Dataset orchestrator and evidence-architecture service for LLM hosts.
mcp_end_state.principle: The MCP should not merely return data. It should tell an LLM what evidence exists, how it can be combined, what has been validated, what remains missing, and which representation templates fit the result.
flow: user describes idea in ChatGPT/Claude/other host
LLM asks DataFit MCP for evidence plan
MCP returns source-backed dataset candidates and roles
MCP optionally executes bounded deterministic operations
MCP returns analysis plan and RepresentationSpec options
user's LLM host or browser renders/generates the final artefact
mcp_end_state.compute_model: Data intelligence and bounded validation can run in the service; expensive generative rendering stays with the user/client where possible.

catalogue.pagination_rule: ordered pagination is required for stable complete catalogue loading

important_dataset_findings: Baumkronenbedeckung is a table of raster download links, not a directly intersectable vector canopy layer.
The obvious Baustellen dataset lacks usable geometry; Allmendbewilligungen provides usable permit polygons for construction/public-space analysis.
Some air-quality datasets are sparse single-site measurements and can be analytically incompatible with city-network questions.
Structural compatibility can be misleading: high-confidence nearest proposals against sparse cycle-route geometry were rejected by execution.

moments: Show the complete live Basel catalogue and navigate it through Atlas projections.
Switch between Topic, Space, Time and Readiness to show the same catalogue as different projections.
Enter a civic use case and show the catalogue reorganize as direct/supporting/contextual/missing evidence.
Select two datasets and show a compatibility proposal.
Validate one relationship with real data and show either confirmation or rejection.
Offer two or three recommended representation templates for the resulting evidence.

submission_positioning.suggested_title: Open Data Explorer — A navigable atlas for Basel-Stadt Open Data
submission_positioning.suggested_description: A use-case-first exploration layer for Basel-Stadt's Open Government Data catalogue. The prototype organizes the live catalogue into navigable thematic, spatial, temporal and readiness views, helps users discover datasets from real-world questions, evaluates whether selected datasets can actually be combined, and recommends useful visual forms for the result. Rather than replacing the official portal, it adds an exploratory and analytical layer on top of its APIs.
submission_positioning.datasets_to_list_in_showcase: List the concrete datasets used in the curated demo executions rather than all catalogue records.

future_extensions: Cloudflare Worker for catalogue snapshots and change history
multi-catalogue adapters such as opendata.swiss or Zürich
